column1: # THE LINCHPIN PROBE: does correlated row explosion exist?
# H2's fatal wall (H2_BACKEND.md §4, D1) was that no H2 version has LATERAL and no
# correlated FROM form works. If a backend HAS correlated explosion, the whole LIST_*
# family is reachable by rewrite and the H2 conclusion does NOT transfer.
# Cross-dialect on purpose — each backend is expected to fail the other's forms.

column3: SELECT e.id, u.v FROM (SELECT 1 AS id, ARRAY[10,20,30] AS arr) e, unnest(e.arr) AS u(v) ORDER BY u.v LIMIT 1
SELECT e.id, u.v FROM (SELECT 1 AS id, ARRAY[10,20,30] AS arr) e, LATERAL unnest(e.arr) AS u(v) ORDER BY u.v LIMIT 1
SELECT e.id, u.v FROM (SELECT 1 AS id, ARRAY[10,20,30] AS arr) e CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(e.arr) AS u(v) ORDER BY u.v LIMIT 1
SELECT e.id, u.v FROM (SELECT 1 AS id, ARRAY[10,20,30] AS arr) e LEFT JOIN LATERAL unnest(e.arr) AS u(v) ON TRUE ORDER BY u.v LIMIT 1
SELECT unnest(ARRAY[10,20,30]) AS v ORDER BY v LIMIT 1
SELECT (SELECT sum(u.v) FROM unnest(e.arr) AS u(v)) FROM (SELECT ARRAY[10,20,30] AS arr) e
SELECT e.id, (SELECT count(*) FROM unnest(e.arr) x) FROM (SELECT 1 AS id, ARRAY[10,20,30] AS arr) e
SELECT e.id, j.value FROM (SELECT 1 AS id, '[10,20,30]' AS arr) e, json_each(e.arr) j ORDER BY j.value LIMIT 1
SELECT e.id, j.value FROM (SELECT 1 AS id, '[10,20,30]' AS arr) e JOIN json_each(e.arr) j ORDER BY j.value LIMIT 1
SELECT value FROM json_each('[10,20,30]') ORDER BY value LIMIT 1
SELECT (SELECT sum(value) FROM json_each(e.arr)) FROM (SELECT '[10,20,30]' AS arr) e
SELECT count(*) FROM json_tree('[10,20,30]')
SELECT json_group_array(value) FROM json_each('[10,20,30]')
SELECT jt.v FROM (SELECT 1 AS id, '[10,20,30]' AS arr) e, JSON_TABLE(e.arr, '$[*]' COLUMNS (v INT PATH '$')) AS jt ORDER BY jt.v LIMIT 1
SELECT JSON_EXTRACT('[10,20,30]', '$[1]')
SELECT JSON_LENGTH('[10,20,30]')
SELECT JSON_ARRAYAGG(id) FROM dept

column1: # --- Row-correlated explosion against a REAL table (the shape that actually matters) ---

column3: SELECT d.id, u.v FROM dept d, LATERAL unnest(ARRAY[d.id, d.id*10]) AS u(v) ORDER BY d.id, u.v LIMIT 1
SELECT d.id, j.value FROM dept d, json_each('[' || d.id || ',' || (d.id*10) || ']') j ORDER BY d.id, j.value LIMIT 1
SELECT d.id, jt.v FROM dept d, JSON_TABLE(CONCAT('[', d.id, ',', d.id*10, ']'), '$[*]' COLUMNS (v INT PATH '$')) jt ORDER BY d.id, jt.v LIMIT 1
